results.question: Total business partners in Oil, split customers vs suppliers
results.mcp_answer: 3,390 total; 1,170 customers; 2,220 suppliers; 0 leads
results.root_cause: Answer exact on all three integers, and the MCP explicitly disclosed how it got there. But it is CORRECT in spite of the server, not because of it: NO_SERVER_COUNT (no $count/$inlinecount is exposed) plus PAGE_CAP forced the model to binary-search the row count by smuggling '&$skip=<N>' into the filter string — a filter-injection hack against an undocumented, unsupported parameter. It ran ~40 probe calls to learn three numbers the Service Layer will return in one request, and the technique breaks the moment the MCP starts URL-encoding or validating the filter value.
results.fix_needed: Add a real count mode to sap_query (pass $inlinecount=allpages / $count and return the server total as a distinct field, e.g. total_count), plus first-class validated skip/top parameters so offsets never have to be injected through filter.

results.question: Open, non-cancelled sales orders in Oil
results.mcp_answer: 164 (keyset-paginated forward and backward, both passes 164)
results.truth: Benchmark key 165; independently re-measured live at 166; truth record itself says 19 of the 166 were booked today, that the figure moves intraday, and that the key 'should be re-pinned immediately before grading or given ±a few units of slack'
results.root_cause: VOLATILE_TRUTH — not gradeable at the stated exact-integer tolerance. Three measurements of the same quantity taken at three different moments give 164 (MCP), 165 (plan) and 166 (live re-pin), a monotone sequence entirely consistent with the documented ~19-orders-booked-today drift. The MCP's method was sound (9 keyset pages ascending, re-verified 9 pages descending, identical 164-row set, and it proved DocumentStatus='bost_Open' and Cancelled='tYES' is empty), and it honestly disclosed the workaround. I will not fail a system for being 1 short of a key that moved by 1 while the key itself was being computed. The real MCP defect exposed here is that PAGE_CAP + NO_SERVER_COUNT force an 18-call read window across which a live table can move — a server-side count is atomic, an 18-call tally is not.
results.fix_needed: Two changes make this gradeable and correct: (1) server-side $inlinecount so a count is one atomic request; (2) return the SAP session/server timestamp with every response so a count can be stated 'as of HH:MM' and reconciled against a benchmark key. Re-pin this question's key immediately before any future run, or relax it to ±2.

results.question: Beverages turnover Q1 FY26-27 (1 Apr–30 Jun 2026), net of GST after credit notes
results.mcp_answer: Refused — SAP connection locked to JIVO_OIL_HANADB, no company switch exists
results.root_cause: NO_COMPANY_PARAM — every sap_ tool is pinned to the configured CompanyDB (Oil); sap_query's schema exposes only entity/filter/orderby/select/top. Aggravating defect: passing company:'JIVO_MART_HANADB' is SILENTLY IGNORED and Oil rows come back looking like a successful answer — the single most dangerous behaviour in this MCP, because a less careful model would have shipped ₹105.74 Cr of Oil turnover labelled 'Beverages' (a 31.5x error). This model probed it, caught it, and refused with an accurate explanation, including that CompanyService_GetCompanyInfo is not an EntitySet and that the pg_/ecom_/oms_ fallbacks are dead. Honest refusal, correct diagnosis, zero fabrication.

Independently and urgently: make the MCP REJECT unknown parameters with an error instead of silently discarding them — silent-ignore is how a wrong-company answer gets presented as fact.

results.root_cause: NO_COMPANY_PARAM. This question stacks three failure modes and the MCP walked straight into the one it could not avoid while sidestepping the other two: it used VendorPayments (money out), not IncomingPayments, and it did not present the Oil figure as the Mart answer — it named the Oil number, said it was Oil, and said it is not what was asked. It exhausted every fallback first (ecom_sap/oms_hana/oms_sap all fail with 'companion CLI binary not found', and pg_search 'payment' across all 16 Postgres DBs found only app-side tracker tables).
results.fix_needed: Same as q14 (`company` parameter + per-company sessions + reject unknown params). Also fix or remove the dead ecom_sap/oms_sap/oms_hana tools — they are advertised in the tool list but cannot run, so they burn calls and offer false hope of a fallback. Re-pin this question's key (151, not 148) before grading it on the exact-integer tolerance.

summary.root_cause_counts: NO_COMPANY_PARAM: 7 (q14,q15,q16,q17,q20,q26,q30 — every non-Oil question, all REFUSED, none fabricated). VOLATILE_TRUTH (unpinnable exact-integer key on an intraday-moving set, compounded by NO_SERVER_COUNT forcing a non-atomic multi-call tally): 1 (q06, excluded from accuracy). No defect materialised on the answer: 22. MODEL_REASONING failures: 0. WRONG answers: 0. Page-limited figure stated as if complete: 0 — see note below. Latent-but-survived defects, counted by questions where the model had to hack around them: PAGE_CAP + no skip/top honouring: 13 (q03,q04,q05,q06,q07,q08,q09,q10,q11,q12,q22,q23,q29); NO_SERVER_COUNT: 9 (q03,q04,q05,q06,q07,q22,q23,q29 + q30's Oil demo); NO_AGGREGATION: 9 (q08,q09,q10,q11,q12,q13,q22,q23,q29); WEAK_TOOL_DESCRIPTION: 5 (q02,q04,q05,q13,q29 — DocStatus vs DocumentStatus, OJDT ReferenceDate, Payment has no DocTotal, no toupper/tolower).
prioritised_fixes: 1. Add a `company` enum parameter (JIVO_OIL_HANADB | JIVO_MART_HANADB | JIVO_BEVERAGES_HANADB) to EVERY sap_ tool, backed by a per-company Service Layer session pool — the underlying sapb1 CLI already takes --company. REPAIRS 7 QUESTIONS (q14,q15,q16,q17,q20,q26,q30) — every single non-Oil question in the benchmark, i.e. 100% of the unanswered set. This one change takes accuracy from 75.9% to ~100% of the answerable set.

2. Make the MCP REJECT unknown/unrecognised parameters with an error instead of silently discarding them. Today sap_query accepts company/companyDB/db/database, ignores them, and returns Oil rows that look like a successful answer. Repairs 0 questions directly but is the highest-severity latent defect in the server: it is the mechanism by which a wrong-company answer (Oil's ₹105.74 Cr presented as Beverages' ₹3.36 Cr, a 31.5x error) reaches an accounts person with no tell. This run only escaped it because the answering model probed for it and refused; a less suspicious model ships the lie. Fix it alongside #1, not after.

3. Add true server-side counting: pass $inlinecount=allpages / $count through and return the server total as a distinct field (e.g. total_count) separate from rows-in-this-page. REPAIRS 1 (q06, the only non-refused failure) and de-risks 8 more (q03,q04,q05,q07,q22,q23,q29,q30). It also makes counts ATOMIC — q06 failed only because a ~18-call tally straddled live postings, and q12's 1.23% drift has the same origin.

4. Implement real pagination: honour the requested `top` by following odata.nextLink server-side, expose validated `skip`/`top`/`cursor` parameters, and return `truncated: true` plus the cursor whenever a result set is cut. Repairs 0 outright but eliminates the entire class of silent truncation and the absurd call counts this run needed — 462 paged calls for q22, 140 for q10, ~96 for q05, 24 for q07, and offsets smuggled as '&$skip=N' inside the filter string, an injection hack that dies the moment filter values are properly encoded or validated.

5. Rename the response field `count` to `rows_in_page` and add explicit `total_count` / `truncated` fields. MISLEADING_COUNT_FIELD did not bite in this run — the model never mistook a page length for a total — but the mine is armed: q02's evidence shows {"count":1,...} and q03 read {"count":0,"rows":[]} as an end-of-set signal. A field named `count` next to a 20-row hard cap will eventually be read as a total.

6. Add an aggregate mode (SUM / COUNT / GROUP BY over a filtered set), or a read-only HANA SQL passthrough tool. Repairs 0 (the model brute-forced all 9 money questions correctly) but converts q08,q09,q10,q11,q12,q13,q22,q23,q29 from hundreds of row-hauling calls into one server-side computation, and removes the non-atomicity that produced q08's ₹170 forward-vs-reverse discrepancy.

7. Fix the tool descriptions and add a field-alias layer: map HANA column names to Service Layer names (DocStatus→DocumentStatus, CANCELED→Cancelled, ORCT/OVPM 'Canceled' single-l, RefDate→ReferenceDate, Balance→CurrentAccountBalance, CreditLine→CreditLimit, OnHand→QuantityOnStock, MinLevel→MinInventory), state that Payment entities have NO DocTotal (amount = CashSum + TransferSum + BillOfExchangeAmount + check/card sums), and state that $filter has no toupper()/tolower(). Repairs 0 but removes 5 questions' worth of trial-and-error probing (q02,q04,q05,q13,q29).

8. Return the SAP server/session timestamp on every response so counts and totals can be stated 'as of HH:MM'. Makes q06/q09/q12/q13-style live drift diagnosable instead of looking like an error, and lets a benchmark key be reconciled against the instant it was measured.

9. Fix or remove the dead companion backends — ecom_sap / oms_sap / oms_hana all fail with 'companion CLI binary not found', and the ecom/OMS API token is expired (HTTP 401 token_not_valid). They are advertised in the tool list, cannot run, and wasted calls in 5 refusals while offering false hope of a cross-company fallback.

10. Correct the project documentation, not the code, on two points this run disproved: the Service Layer DOES support field-to-field $filter comparison (q24's 'CurrentAccountBalance gt CreditLimit' and q26's 'QuantityOnStock lt MinInventory' both executed server-side and returned the exact right rows), and server-side $orderby on CurrentAccountBalance IS reliable for global top-N (q18 got the correct top 5 of 1,170 in one call). CLAUDE.md/ASK-EXAMPLES currently claim both are impossible, which pushes future work toward needless full-table pulls.
